summary.name: CRE Life Lessons: Why should your app get SRE support?
summary.one_liner: A Google Cloud Blog article by Customer Reliability Engineer Adrian Hilton on how a company should decide which applications its SRE team supports and when to hand support back to developers.
use_cases: deciding which services an SRE team should support
setting a sustainable on-call rotation size
limiting ops work to avoid burnout
deciding when developers should own pager duty
summary.what_it_does: The article describes practical limits on how many applications one SRE team can support, citing a rule of thumb of six engineers minimum for a 24/7 pager rotation with primary and secondary roles. It argues that services not explicitly supported by SRE should be supported by their developer team, and that SREs should not take operational responsibility just because developers are overloaded. It discusses prioritizing services by business criticality while noting that mature, rarely changed infrastructure services may not need SRE support. It lists seven SRE focus areas: monitoring, emergency response, capacity planning, service turn-up/turn-down, change management, performance, and data integrity.
notable: Describes Google's rule of thumb of six engineers minimum per pager rotation and a 12-hour cap on continuous on-call
Warns that teams above 50% ops work tend to slide toward 100% ops, losing project capacity
Lists seven SRE focus areas that developers typically do not cover
caveats: This is an opinion and experience article, not a product; it describes Google's internal practices
Part 1 of a series; parts 2 and 3 are referenced but not included in this page
